patterns.name: Yellow is an amount, not a mood
patterns.rule: Brand yellow is confined to the CTA fill, the hero statistic, the active-tab underline and a few links; it never fills a section or sets body copy.
patterns.goal: On a page showing dozens of numbers, yellow can only mean 'this is the figure' or 'this is the action'.

patterns.name: Yellow expands with density
patterns.rule: Yellow fill is 0.3% of the marketing home page and 5.3% of the trading floor.
patterns.goal: Marketing reads dark with a highlight; the trading product reads brand-forward because product mode replaces marketing mode.

patterns.name: Three dark layers, no shadows
patterns.rule: Canvas #181A20, card #29313D, well #1E2329, separated by #333B47 hairlines; a single shadow exists in the sample.
patterns.goal: Depth survives on OLED and dim screens without blur halos over 12px price text.

patterns.name: Numbers get the largest type
patterns.rule: The hero figure is 72px while headlines are 40px and body 12px — a 6x ratio between statistic and prose.
patterns.goal: A reader scanning for a number never hunts; hierarchy is data > headline > body.

patterns.name: One UI family, one earned display face
patterns.rule: BinanceNova carries every surface; BinancePlex appears on 10 nodes in 2 of 4 pages.
patterns.goal: Keeps product pages uniform while letting campaign pages differ slightly.

patterns.name: A two-colour direction axis
patterns.rule: Gains use #2EBD85 and losses #F6465D, always as text, never as a filled badge.
patterns.goal: Direction stays legible at 12px without competing with the brand yellow.

patterns.name: Radii track role
patterns.rule: Buttons 10px, cards and tabs 8px, large option tiles 16px, inline chips 4px.
patterns.goal: Silhouette alone tells a card from a button from a tile.

patterns.name: Hover is fast, panels are slow
patterns.rule: Colour and border hovers run at 0.15-0.2s; panel and image transforms at 0.7s.
patterns.goal: Interface feedback is immediate while promotional movement stays calm enough to read.

taste.name: Colour is assigned by role, not by hierarchy
taste.trigger: Designing a screen that shows prices, price changes, actions and promotions at once.
taste.decision: One accent for brand and action, green/red for direction, blue-greys for everything else.
taste.chose: a three-role colour system (brand, direction, neutral)
taste.over: a hue per category (per-coin colours, per-section accents, coloured badges)
taste.reason: In a list of fifty numbers, a colour that could mean anything stops carrying meaning; three roles keep a glance reliable.

taste.name: Depth is a hairline, not a shadow
taste.trigger: Layering cards and inputs on a near-black canvas.
taste.decision: Separate layers with #333B47 1px borders over a #29313D fill; one shadow exists in the whole sample.
taste.over: a drop shadow on every card and panel
taste.reason: On a dark canvas a shadow is invisible until it is strong enough to smear the 12px digits sitting on it.

guardrail.note: Exception: the single floating overlay panel measured at 14px/6px blur. Everything else is a 1px border.

taste.name: Data outranks copy
taste.trigger: Deciding what to enlarge on a landing page that also has to sell a product.
taste.decision: Scale the statistic to 72px, the headline to 40px/600, prose to 12px.
taste.over: a balanced 48/28/16 marketing scale where copy and data compete
taste.reason: The promise of an exchange is a number; making it the largest object lets a screenshot-free page still read as a product.

taste.name: The display face is earned, not standard
taste.trigger: Choosing type families across marketing and trading surfaces.
taste.decision: BinanceNova everywhere; BinancePlex only on 10 nodes in 2 of 4 pages.
taste.chose: a single UI family with a sparing display face
taste.reason: A second family used everywhere splits product identity from marketing; used sparingly it signals that this surface is different.

guardrail.note: A display face is allowed only on campaign blocks, never on tables, prices or controls.
